drafted_by: AI, requires clinician review before any real use.

questions.text: What part of your life is affecting your health right now: smoking, alcohol, drugs, work, money, housing, stress, or safety at home?
questions.rationale: Clarifying the main social concern guides the next branch of the interview.

questions.text: Who do you live with, and is your housing stable?
questions.rationale: Living situation affects support, follow-up, and discharge planning.

questions.text: In the past year, have you been without a steady place to sleep, or worried about losing your housing?
questions.rationale: Housing instability changes the feasibility of treatment plans.

questions.text: In the past year, have you worried that food would run out before you had money to buy more?
questions.rationale: Food insecurity affects nutrition, diabetes control, and medication timing.

questions.text: What kind of work do you do, and are you exposed to chemicals, dust, noise, heavy lifting, or long shifts?
questions.rationale: Occupation drives exposures, injury risk, and ability to follow a treatment plan.

questions.text: Do you smoke cigarettes, cigars, or a pipe, or have you in the past? How much and for how long?
questions.rationale: Pack-year history drives cancer, lung, and heart disease risk.

questions.text: Do you vape or use cannabis? How often, and how do you use it?
questions.rationale: Vaping and cannabis carry lung, mood, and interaction risks.

questions.text: How many days a week do you drink alcohol, and how many drinks do you have on a typical day?
questions.rationale: Quantifying intake identifies risky drinking.

questions.text: How often do you have five or more drinks (four or more for women) on one occasion?
questions.rationale: Binge drinking is a validated single-item screen for unhealthy alcohol use.

questions.text: Have you ever had shakes, sweats, seeing things, or seizures when you cut back on drinking, or needed a drink first thing in the morning?
questions.rationale: A history of withdrawal predicts dangerous withdrawal and need for monitoring.

questions.text: In the past year, have you used any street drugs or taken prescription medicines in a way not prescribed?
questions.rationale: Drug use changes diagnosis, medication safety, and harm-reduction needs.

questions.text: Have you ever injected drugs, and have you shared needles or other equipment?
questions.rationale: Injection use raises risk of HIV, hepatitis, endocarditis, and overdose.

questions.text: Have you ever overdosed, and do you use opioids alone or have naloxone available?
questions.rationale: Prior overdose and using alone are the strongest predictors of fatal overdose.

questions.text: Within the past year, has anyone hit, kicked, choked, threatened, or controlled you, or do you feel unsafe at home?
questions.rationale: Intimate partner violence is common, under-disclosed, and needs a safety plan.

questions.text: Are there firearms in your home, and are they stored locked and unloaded?
questions.rationale: Firearm access sharply raises the lethality of suicide attempts and violence.

questions.text: Do you depend on someone for care, and has anyone neglected you, taken your money, or hurt you?
questions.rationale: Elder or dependent-adult abuse is often hidden and requires action.

questions.text: Has anyone forced you to work or do things you did not want to do, or taken your ID or pay?
questions.rationale: These are screening signs of labor or sex trafficking.

questions.text: Who can you count on for help, such as family, friends, or a community or faith group?
questions.rationale: Social support affects recovery, adherence, and mental health.

questions.text: How much stress are you under from work, money, relationships, or caregiving?
questions.rationale: Chronic stress contributes to many physical and mental health problems.

questions.text: What does a typical day of eating look like, and how much physical activity do you get each week?
questions.rationale: Diet and activity are core modifiable risk factors.

questions.text: Do you have reliable transportation to appointments and the pharmacy, and can you afford your medicines?
questions.rationale: Transportation and cost barriers are leading causes of missed care.

questions.text: Have you traveled outside the country or to a new area recently?
questions.rationale: Travel history widens the differential for infectious illness.

questions.text: Have you served in the military or spent time in jail or prison?
questions.rationale: Military service and incarceration carry specific exposure, trauma, and infection risks.

questions.text: What is the main thing you are worried this could be?
questions.rationale: Understanding the patient's concern guides reassurance and follow-up questions.

red_flags.label: Unsafe at home or partner violence
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe being hit, choked, threatened, or controlled by a partner, or feeling unsafe at home?

red_flags.label: Risk of alcohol withdrawal
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe heavy daily drinking with past shakes, hallucinations, or seizures when cutting back, or drinking in the morning?

red_flags.label: High overdose risk
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report a past overdose, using opioids alone, or using fentanyl or pills from an unknown source?

red_flags.label: Injection drug use
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient report injecting drugs or sharing needles or equipment?

red_flags.label: Possible elder or dependent-adult abuse
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient who depends on a caregiver describe neglect, financial exploitation, or being hurt?

red_flags.label: Possible labor or sex trafficking
red_flags.detection_instructions: Does the patient describe being forced to work or perform acts, having ID or pay withheld, or being unable to leave?
